# Connector matrix

What Koan plugs into, on one screen. Use it to answer "can this talk to X?" without reading
the capability map. Once the answer is yes, the map carries the exact package and its recipe.

| Family | Providers |
|---|---|
| Entity store | Cockroach · Couchbase · CouchDb · DuckDb · Elasticsearch · Firebird · InMemory · Json · Mongo · MySql · OpenSearch · Postgres · Redis · SQL Server · SQLite |
| Vector index | Chroma · InMemory · Milvus · MongoAtlasVector ⚠ · PgVector ⚠ · Qdrant · RedisVector ⚠ · SqliteVec · Weaviate |
| AI runtime | Hugging Face ⚠ · LlamaCpp · LM Studio · Ollama · ONNX |
| Object storage | Local · S3 ⚠ |
| Cache tier | Redis ⚠ · SQLite |
| Sign-in provider | Atproto ⚠ · Discord · Google · Microsoft · Test |
| Message transport | RabbitMQ |

**⚠ carries no product claim.** It is installable and documented, and nothing has been promised
about it. Say so plainly when recommending one; the
[capability map](capability-map.md) records why each is listed, and the
[product surface](product-surface.md) is the evaluated authority.

A family with one provider, or one unclaimed provider, is a real constraint on what an
application can be deployed against. Read the short rows as carefully as the long ones.

This page does not list what Koan cannot reach — the ranked gaps and the reasoning behind them
belong to [ARCH-0127](../decisions/ARCH-0127-connector-fleet-strategy.md).
